root_motivation: The fleet's recurring jobs (vibeloop tick + measure, self-review, digest timers, and the incoming janitor and beacon) are placed by hand: a unit enabled on one node, a script edited locally on another. The vibeloop tick's RedBaron placement exists only as a local edit to `claude-vibeloop-tick.sh` — invisible to fleet-sync, unrecoverable on re-image, and silently duplicable (a second node enabling the same timer would double-run the loop against one repo and one hub). Nobody can answer "what is supposed to run where" without ssh-ing into every node and listing timers.
user_persona: UNSPECIFIED — onboarded without a PRD or a 5-Whys interview; set by hand or by the next PRD that lands on this crate.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given placement.toml assigns vibeloop-tick to redbaron, When `wm-node should-run vibeloop-tick` runs on redbaron, Then exit 0; and on carbon, Then exit 1.
Given the populated placement.toml, When `wm-node assignments --format json` runs, Then every entry appears with its node and a boolean marking local assignment.
Given a unit enabled locally for a job assigned elsewhere, When `wm-node doctor` runs, Then the job is listed under misplaced-enabled and doctor exits 1.
Given a job assigned here with no enabled unit, When doctor runs, Then it is listed under assigned-but-disabled and doctor exits 1.
Given all assigned jobs enabled and no strays, When doctor runs, Then it reports healthy and exits 0.

Given the vibeloop timer units in the dotfiles repo, When the build lands, Then each carries an ExecCondition wm-node should-run line and no local-only placement edit remains on RedBaron. Deferred per PRD-wm-node-loop-placement.md's deferred_acs line + agent/intent_card_amendment_request.json: editing the dotfiles repo's unit sources is a different repo's job, one this crate doesn't own; wm-node's own mechanism (should-run, assignments, doctor) is done, ready for that follow-on edit to consume.
Given placement.toml is absent, When `wm-node should-run anything` runs, Then exit 0 with a stderr warning; and When doctor runs, Then it reports the missing file and exits 1.
Given a job assigned to ryzen7 flagged may-be-off, When assignments renders, Then the entry carries the may-be-off annotation.
Given a duplicate job key in placement.toml, When doctor runs, Then it exits 2 naming the duplicate key.
Given one misplaced and one missing unit, When `wm-node doctor --fix` runs, Then it prints the exact disable and enable commands and executes neither.
